name: Kalamatianos
notes: Kalamatianos style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first, alone-together). Greece's default celebration dance — the open-circle dance in 7/8 that every wedding, baptism and panigiri (village festival) reaches for, named for Kalamata and standing on the ancient syrtos family (circle dances appear in antiquity's records; claims of unbroken continuity are told as lineage-with-humility, not proof). THE SEVEN is the pack's gift: kalamatianos runs 7/8 counted 3+2+2 — slow-quick-quick — and it now lives in this app's Rhythm Trainer; owning an odd meter re-tunes your ear for every dance you'll ever learn. Design truths: the 12-step pattern is genuinely solo-trainable; the CIRCLE is the dance — group-flagged 🤝 with its etiquette (the leader improvises at the head holding the mantili/handkerchief, everyone else holds the step; join the open circle at the END); Greek diaspora communities worldwide keep festival floors open to everyone.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping and stepping the 7/8 — slow-quick-quick — through one full kalamatianos. The seven, owned.
Film the 12-step pattern traveling right — light, lifted, restarting cleanly with the phrase.
Film the pattern with the lift and the light cross-behinds styled in — buoyant, never bouncy.
Film the pattern in circle position — arms at shoulder height as if holding neighbors, traveling the arc.
Join a real circle — a Greek festival, a wedding, a taverna night, a Greek school glendi. Join at the open end; the circle teaches.

attributes.name: Odd-meter ear L2
attributes.test: clap 3+2+2 through one full kalamatianos without collapsing it into square time — the seven must stay seven

attributes.name: Light-step ankles L1
attributes.test: 90s of light lifted stepping on the balls of the feet, landings quiet, calves easy after

nodes.name: The seven — 3+2+2
checkpoints: kalamatianos runs 7/8, counted as ONE-two-three, ONE-two, ONE-two — slow-quick-quick; it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
say it as Greeks teach it: 'kal-a-ma — tia — nos' fits the bar
an odd meter owned once re-tunes the ear forever — this is the pack's real payload, like son's contratiempo

nodes.name: The songbook — from Samiotissa outward
checkpoints: a shared songbook powers the circle — 'Samiotissa' and 'Milo Mou Kokkino' are the gateway classics; learn to hear their phrases
clarinet, laouto, violin and voice trade the lead; the 7/8 never blinks
syrtos cousins in other meters (kalamatianos' slower 4/4 relatives) share the family floor — recognize them before dancing them

nodes.name: The syrtos family — ancient-rooted, worn daily
checkpoints: kalamatianos stands on the syrtos family — 'dragging' circle dances; circle dances appear in Greek antiquity's records, and the continuity claims are told as lineage-with-humility, not laboratory proof
named for Kalamata (the song lineage 'Mantili Kalamatiano' — the Kalamata kerchief — carried the name)
it is Greece's default celebration dance: weddings, baptisms, panigiria, national days — the circle everyone's grandmother expects you to join

nodes.name: Circle etiquette — the leader, the mantili, the open end
checkpoints: the circle is OPEN: a leader dances the right-hand end, free to improvise — lifts, slaps, kneels — often connected by a mantili (handkerchief) to the second dancer who anchors them
everyone else holds the step and the line; the leadership rotates as dancers peel to the head across a night
join at the open END, match the step, hold your neighbors' hands at shoulder height — three rules, lifelong welcome

nodes.name: Stepping the seven
checkpoints: weight changes ride the 3+2+2: a long settled step on the slow, two light steps on the quicks
in place first — the meter in the legs before any pattern
light and lifted: Greek circle style floats; landings whisper
mistakes: squaring the seven into marching eighths (the music will fight you and win)

nodes.name: The 12-step pattern
nodes.anchor: the pattern that joins every Greek celebration on earth
checkpoints: twelve steps over four bars, traveling RIGHT: walks forward in the line's direction, a cross-behind, a point-and-return that gathers you for the restart
the pattern breathes with the 7/8 phrase and restarts seamlessly — no seam, no stutter
eyes up and around the circle-to-be; this dance is danced facing company
restart cleanly from anywhere — at a real panigiri you'll join mid-tune, always
mistakes: watching your feet (the circle's whole point is the faces)
traveling left (the circle flows right; swim with it)

nodes.name: Lift & styling
checkpoints: the buoyant lift on the slow count — a rise through the ball of the foot, never a hop
light cross-behinds and a small kick-point sell the quicks
styling stays inside the line's discipline; only the LEADER's end earns the fireworks

nodes.name: Circle position (solo prep)
checkpoints: dance the pattern with arms raised to shoulder height as if holding neighbors' hands — the W hold, rehearsed solo
shoulders stay easy while the arms hold; your hands must be good neighbors (the dabke pack's line-prep is this drill's cousin)
travel a wide arc, not a straight line — you are one bead of a circle

nodes.name: The circle (with people)
checkpoints: join at the open end, take the hand offered, match the step by watching feet ACROSS the circle (easier than beside you)
hold the line steady when the leader flies — your steadiness is what makes their flight possible
weddings, panigiria, Greek school glendia, taverna nights: the diaspora keeps circles open on every continent

nodes.name: Two songs, unbroken — filmed
checkpoints: two kalamatianos songs back to back — pattern traveling, styling alive, restarts invisible, the seven never squared
arms in circle position for at least one full song
the test is joining-readiness: could a stranger's circle absorb you mid-phrase? Film says yes or no

nodes.name: The panigiri
checkpoints: find the circle: a Greek festival, a wedding you're invited to, a Greek Orthodox community's glendi, a taverna with live music
join at the open end; let the circle correct you kindly (it will, and it means welcome)
when the leader takes the mantili and flies, hold your piece of the line and understand: alone-together, in seven
